The '''Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival (JRMF)''' is an educational organization that sponsors locally organized mathematics festivals and online webinars targeting K–12 students. The events are designed to introduce students to mathematics in a collaborative and non-competitive forum.<ref name=huffing/><ref name=MSRI>[https://www.msri.org/web/msri/education/for-k-12-educators/julia-robinson-math-festival Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival] [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]]</ref><ref name=about>[https://jrmf.org/about/ About Us] jrmf.org</ref>

==History==
In the 1970s, [[Saint Mary's College of California]] produced a mathematics contest that was popular with secondary schools throughout the [[San Francisco Bay Area]].<ref name=marycontest>[https://www.amazon.com/College-Mathematics-Contest-Problems-Junior/dp/B01LBHKVLS Saint Mary's College Mathematics Contest Problems For Junior and Senior High School]</ref>  In 2005, Nancy Blachman attended an education forum sponsored by the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI) and remembered how the Saint Mary's contest had inspired her as a student.<ref name=SMMC>[https://www.gathering4gardner.org/g4g12gift/Blachman_Nancy-Saint_Marys_Math.pdf Saint Mary's Math Contest: High School Division] : by Nancy Blachman & Nick Baxter</ref> Unfortunately, the contest no longer existed.  Seeking to possibly resurrect the contest, Blachman and MSRI development director Jim Sotiros reached out to colleagues in the educational community.  One response was from local high school math teacher Joshua Zucker, who also remembered the contest and even had saved a book of problems from it.<ref name=MSRI/>  Sotiros suggested that Blachman and her husband David desJardins fund MSRI in order to hire Zucker to recreate a program in the style of the Saint Mary's Math Contest.  Blachman and Zucker became co-founders and organized their first event in 2007.<ref>[http://mathforum.org/t2t/bios/zucker.html Joshua Zucker] Math Forum</ref><ref name=first/>  They called it a festival rather than a contest because they wanted to emphasize collaboration, creativity and fun rather than competition.<ref name=MSRI/> They named the festival after [[Julia Robinson]], a mathematician renowned for her contributions to [[decision problems]].  In fact, her work on [[Hilbert's 10th problem]] played a crucial role in its ultimate resolution.<ref name="Julia">
{{cite book
|last= Reid
|first= Constance
|title= Julia: A life in mathematics
|url= https://archive.org/details/julialifeinmathe0000reid
|url-access= registration
|year= 1996
|publisher=Mathematical Association of America
|location=Washington, DC
|isbn=0-88385-520-8
}}
</ref>  Blachman felt that such a woman would provide a role model for young girls and would show that one need not be male to be a great mathematician.<ref name=huffing>"[https://www.huffingtonpost.com/colm-mulcahy/getting-kids-excited-abou_b_3343079.html Getting Kids Excited About Mathematics, One Festival at a Time]" By [[Colm Mulcahy]], [[Huffington Post]] Blog, December 6, 2017</ref>

When they sent out invitations to local schools, the response was so overwhelming that, in order to have enough space, they prevailed upon [[Google]] in nearby [[Mountain View, California|Mountain View]] to host the first festival.<ref name=first>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qDL7yoz1TGQ The 2007 Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival at Google was the founding of this event for middle school and high school students.] video</ref> A second festival was hosted in 2008 by [[Pixar Animation Studios]] in [[Emeryville, California|Emeryville]].<ref>[https://www.jrmf.org/history/ History of JRMF] By Nancy Blachman, JRMF Founder</ref> Enthusiasm and interest have spurred strong growth, and since then, there have been festivals at [[Princeton University]] (and its greater community); [[Stanford University]]; and [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref>[https://www.pastfoundation.org/jrm julia robinson mathematics festival at past]</ref> and throughout the United States,<ref>[https://uknow.uky.edu/uk-happenings/uk-mathematics-hosts-julia-robinson-math-festival UK Mathematics Hosts Julia Robinson Math Festival] By Jenny Wells, [[University of Kentucky]], October 30, 2017</ref> as well as in Europe and Asia.<ref>[https://www.algebragamification.com/jrmf/ The Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival in Hong Kong], March 24, 2018</ref>

As of December 2019, JRMF will have hosted nearly 500 events in 25 states, the District of Columbia, one territory (Puerto Rico), and 15 foreign countries. In 2020, they hosted over 120 Festivals—an increase of more than 50% over 2018. The services JRMF offer continue to be free of charge. The Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival has been invited to host festivals and tables at events such as the Joint Mathematics Meeting and MAA Mathfest. In December 2019, they celebrated Julia Robinson's 100th birthday with a festival in her hometown.

==Programming==

The Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival has hosted festivals in over 15 countries and 25 states and territories. 

===COVID-19 Response===

In order to help families cope with COVID-19, the Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival, under the leadership of Hector Rosario, launched the JRMF Webinar Series on March 26, 2020. In this weekly series, they explore an activity that they use at their festivals. In order to serve the national and international communities, they host three sessions of the same seminar every Thursday, from 7 AM to 7 PM EDT, in three languages - English, Spanish and Hebrew. Participants from the US, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East come to attend. Many community members and volunteers have joined the JRMF team as facilitators to lead breakout rooms in order to provide closer attention to each participant for learning and brainstorming.

==Support==
Since its founding, JRMF has had the support of many people and organizations, including dedicated mentors and volunteers, the founding host MSRI, and the [[American Institute of Mathematics]] (AIM), which has been a fiscal sponsor since 2013.  JRMF has also frequently partnered with various educational, corporate, and mathematical organizations including The [[Math Circle|National Association of Math Circles]], The [[National Museum of Mathematics]], [[ThinkFun]], and [[Gathering 4 Gardner]] (G4G). Among The "Friends of JRMF" are [[David Eisenbud]], [[Gary Antonick]], [[Peter Norvig]], [[Vi Hart]], and [[Megan Smith]].<ref name=sponsors>[https://www.jrmf.org/partnerships Sponsors and Partners] JRMF.org</ref>
